mainEntity.name: Does this include state income tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Optionally. Choose a state with no income tax, a flat-rate state, or enter your own effective state rate. Federal tax is modeled with the exact 2026 brackets; the state figure is an estimate.

mainEntity.name: Does this account for deductions or credits?

acceptedAnswer.text: It models the standard or itemized deduction and pre-tax 401(k), HSA and Section 125 contributions. It doesn't model tax credits, so your actual tax may be lower if you qualify for any.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between taxable income and gross income?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gross income is total earnings before any adjustments; taxable income is what remains after subtracting deductions (standard or itemized) and other adjustments — it's the taxable income figure that tax brackets actually apply to.

mainEntity.name: Why did my tax bill differ from this estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is a simplified estimate — actual tax bills are affected by credits, other income types, state tax rules, and deduction specifics not modeled here.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a tax deduction and a tax credit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A deduction reduces your taxable income before tax is calculated. A credit reduces your final tax bill dollar-for-dollar, making credits generally more valuable than deductions of the same size.
